name: Linux enum
what_it_does: Read-only picture of a Linux or Unix host: system, listening ports and their programs, accounts and groups, services, cron and other autostart, SSH, sudo, privilege escalation paths (like linpeas), risky files, firewall, credentials in config files, containers, processes, connections, sessions, kernel modules, PAM, trust files. One-page summary worst first; profiles card, full, triage. To do: write findings with a fix ID so the matching fix can be run on its own

name: Windows enum
what_it_does: Read-only picture of a Windows host: domain role, accounts and admin/RDP group members, listening ports with programs, services, autostart and backdoor places (Run keys, Winlogon, debugger keys, WMI, sticky keys), tasks, security settings, firewall, Defender, processes, connections, sessions, shares, software, events, drivers. Every source saved raw and replayable. To do: findings with a fix ID

name: AD enum
what_it_does: Read-only look at Active Directory: users, admin groups (nested too), GPOs and logon scripts, risky permissions, service accounts, stored passwords.

name: Web and database enum (Linux)
what_it_does: Asks what to look at, then shows web servers, sites, which URL path serves which folder or app (aliases, proxies, PHP), languages and app servers (PHP, Python, Node, Java, Ruby, .NET, dev servers), web roots with web shells/dumps/.env/.git, risky PHP settings, apps with their database, MySQL/PostgreSQL accounts and data stores. Flags shown live; readable tables and CSVs

name: Network scan
what_it_does: Asks what to scan, then nmap in stages: top 1000 ports, all ports, versions/scripts/vuln on the open ones, UDP. Flags vulns and bad services, summary of ports and vulns; with the host list it checks scored services. Falls back to python, bash or nc without nmap

name: Scan diff
what_it_does: What changed between two network scans or two enum runs of one host, additions first
you_give_it: Two run folders (or the newest two)

name: Network device config audit
what_it_does: Reads saved device configs: telnet or HTTP management, default SNMP communities, weak or clear-text passwords, management open to any, any-to-any rules, default admins. Touches no device

name: Linux backup
what_it_does: Run before any change. Asks which box (offers that box's folders), web roots, homes, extra paths and paths to leave out (typed), and where to copy it; then archives /etc, crontabs, web roots, service configs and home dotfiles with a hash list, snapshots firewall, services and ports, and copies it off the host. Linpeas-style sections, numbered backup-N folders

name: Windows backup
what_it_does: Run before any change. Registry areas, firewall, security and audit policy, tasks, hosts file, users and services; IIS, DNS zones, DHCP; on a DC every GPO, SYSVOL and AD object lists. Restore command per item, hashes, copy off the box

name: Database backup
what_it_does: Dumps every MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL database and SQLite files in web roots; checks each dump reads back; hashes; restore commands; copy off the box. To do: SQL Server

name: Site backup and restore
what_it_does: Backs up each web site (files with a hash of every file, its database from the app config, web server and PHP configs); check lists changed, deleted and new files (web shells HIGH); restore puts back only what changed, quarantines new files and can reload the database, with a revert timer

name: Web shell hunter
what_it_does: Finds web shells by content (request data run as code, eval of encoded code, PHP in uploads or images, .htaccess handlers, changed or extra WordPress core files) with the matching line; quarantines asked per file; site check with one-at-a-time retry; --watch --auto-quarantine

name: Database hardening
what_it_does: Lists every MySQL/MariaDB account and the app that uses it; safe/service/access fixes: anonymous accounts, test database, local_infile, remote root, no-password accounts, FILE right, new app passwords written into the app config, bind to 127.0.0.1, backdoor UDFs. Site checked after; put back if it breaks

name: PHP and web app hardening
what_it_does: Finds the web apps; safe/service/access fixes: PHP settings (allow_url_include, display_errors, expose_php, disable_functions), config files root-only, no PHP in upload folders, block .git/.env/backups and xmlrpc, new WordPress admins kept or demoted, code read-only for the web server. Site checked after; put back if it breaks

name: Webmail (Roundcube) hardening
what_it_does: Roundcube: version vs known holes (CVE-2025-49113, CVE-2024-42009; package changelog read), logins sent to another server, installer, debug that logs passwords, default des_key, log_logins, plugins added later, readable config, downloadable logs/config/SQL; each fix asked; login page checked after

name: Database password rotation
what_it_does: New passwords for every MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL account with one; app configs updated in the same step; each login tested, put back if it fails; site checked after; lock planted accounts. Passwords only in passwords.txt (600)

name: Mail password rotation
what_it_does: New passwords for the mail users wherever Dovecot keeps them (system accounts with a mailbox, passwd-file, Postfix sasldb); each tested by an IMAP login and put back if it fails; flags master and static passdbs. Passwords only in passwords.txt (600)

name: Service recovery
what_it_does: Why is a scored service down: running, masked/disabled, config test, port held by another program, answers like scoring, firewall drops, tampered configs/overrides/package files, disk/tmp/memory; offers each fix (start only on a good config); --watch with --auto-restart

name: Splunk hardening and passwords
what_it_does: Finds Splunk backdoors (scripted inputs, alert scripts, planted apps, deployment server, scripted login, extra admins, default password); new passwords for Splunk users via REST with a login test; disables planted inputs, quarantines apps; restart then a test search, put back if it fails. Not yet run on a real Splunk
you_give_it: Admin login (--auth-file); protected list (the splunk-query user)

name: Gitea hardening
what_it_does: Gitea/Forgejo: open install page (INSTALL_LOCK), sign-ups, git hooks users can add, migrations and webhooks into the inside network, hooks planted in repositories, admin accounts (sqlite), readable app.ini; each fix asked; restart, login page checked after, put back if it breaks

name: File share hardening (Samba and NFS)
what_it_does: Samba: SMB1, NTLMv1/lanman, lines that run programs (root preexec, magic script, ... script), wide links, guest shares anyone can write, force user = root, writable smb.conf; NFS: no_root_squash, insecure, exports open to everyone; each fix asked (guest-write default no); testparm, reload, port 445 and exportfs checked after, put back if it breaks

name: Mail tamper check
what_it_does: Postfix/Dovecot backdoors: hidden BCC copies, delivery programs, rogue master.cf pipe services, open relay, aliases/.forward/procmail that run programs or forward out, sieve execute/redirect, header_checks redirects, post-login scripts, big queue; each fix asked; postfix check, reload, SMTP/IMAP checked after

name: TLS certificate check
what_it_does: Every certificate and key in the Apache, nginx, Dovecot, Postfix, vsftpd and MariaDB configs (expired, wrong key, self-signed, weak key or signature, key others can read) and each TLS port (the certificate really served, TLS 1.0/1.1, weak ciphers). Fingerprint baseline flags a swapped certificate. Fixes: chmod 600, new self-signed pair, TLS 1.2+ config (tested, reloaded, put back if the port stops answering).

name: Service hardening (FTP + legacy)
what_it_does: Hardens insecure services, FTP first (anonymous off, deny system accounts, config perms, chroot), then telnet/rsh/tftp/snmp/legacy inetd. Every action is graded safe/service/access; --level decides how far to go. Dry run, sqlmap questions, service-health check with auto-undo at service level, revert timer at access level. vsftpd fully; proftpd/pure-ftpd reported

name: Network config backup and diff
what_it_does: Saves every firewall, router and switch running config and shows what changed since the last copy
you_give_it: Host list; SSH key or password in an environment variable

name: Linux safe fixes
what_it_does: Only fixes that cannot break a scored service: kernel network settings, file modes on passwd/shadow/sudoers/SSH keys, logging back on, attacker preload and hosts entries reset, trust files removed, extra UID 0 and empty-password accounts locked, SUID removed from GTFOBins programs. Asks a question per fix and what to leave alone (sqlmap style, --batch for defaults, --exclude), shows the plan, applies, then a 2-minute revert timer undoes everything unless kept. --list, --only, --skip; revert.sh per run. To do: read fix IDs from enum findings

name: Windows safe fixes
what_it_does: 20 fixes that cannot break a scored service (WDigest, SMBv1, Zerologon, UAC, Guest, debugger and sticky-keys backdoors, port forwards, Defender, auditing, LM hashes, Winlogon, AppInit, netsh helpers, WMI, hosts, LLMNR). -List, -Only, -Skip, -Undo. To do: move the -Include fixes that can cut off access (NTLM, LSA protection, RDP NLA, SMB signing, firewall) to WN-27 and WN-25; risk label per fix

name: SSH hardening
what_it_does: Shows every SSH key and sshd setting; asks keep or remove for each key and on or off for each setting, with what it does; installs a block at the top of sshd_config tested with sshd -t, reloads, checks sshd still listens, revert timer. Password logins stay on unless you say so

name: Windows firewall
what_it_does: Default-deny inbound; scored, protected and safe listening ports open; admin and scoring addresses allowed; allow-all and backdoor rules off. Rolls back unless kept from a new connection; -Undo restores the old firewall exactly. To do: 1-minute default countdown
you_give_it: Admin addresses; ports to allow or exclude

name: Linux firewall
what_it_does: Shows every open port with the program, account and command behind it and what the port is; asks keep or drop for each; then drops everything else. Own chains only; removed again unless confirmed from a new session
you_give_it: Team addresses; keep or drop per port

name: Windows remote access lockdown
what_it_does: RDP and WinRM lockdown: who can log in, NLA, NTLMv2 only, SMB signing. Each fix runs alone. 1-minute countdown and undo.

name: Remote access lockdown (everything but SSH)
what_it_does: Finds tunnels out (ngrok, chisel, frp, cloudflared, ssh -R), web terminals (ttyd, gotty, shellinabox), bind/reverse shells (nc -e, socat exec, a shell on a socket), remote desktops (VNC, xrdp, NoMachine, TeamViewer, AnyDesk), admin panels (Webmin, Cockpit), quick file servers, database panels; stop or keep each (services disabled, programs killed, files in temp folders quarantined). Scored ports never offered

name: Account lockdown (Windows / AD)
what_it_does: Domain controller: unknown members of the admin groups (removed when -Admins names yours), accounts without Kerberos pre-authentication, password not required, reversible encryption, unconstrained delegation (cleared), new and unapproved accounts and Guest (disabled); SPN accounts, delegated computers and the krbtgt age reported. Each fix asked; revert timer; no Group Policy
you_give_it: Your admin accounts (-Admins); approved users (optional); protected list

name: Account lockdown (Linux)
what_it_does: Every account, one by one: what it can do (UID 0, empty password, admin groups, sudo lines, SSH keys, service accounts with a shell) and keep / lock / take admin away / remove keys / no-login shell; sudo lines that give everyone root commented out (visudo checked). Revert timer and undo

name: Linux password rotation
what_it_does: Lists every account with hidden ones flagged (second UID 0, empty password, hash in /etc/passwd, system account that can log in), then asks per account: random, set (typed, hidden), disable (locked and expired), keep, or all the rest. Protected and current accounts need an extra yes. Plan, apply, then a 5-minute revert timer puts the old passwords back unless kept. New passwords only in a mode-600 file

name: Windows password rotation
what_it_does: New passwords for every enabled local account, or every domain user on a DC; skips service accounts, SPNs, protected and built-in accounts; -Exclude, -Users, -Passwords; each change tested. To do: countdown for the account running it

name: Network device password rotation
what_it_does: Changes the login password on each firewall, router and switch through a kept-open session, tests it from a second session, and puts the old one back if it fails
you_give_it: Host list; current password in an environment variable

name: Device accounts and sessions
what_it_does: Every local admin account on each firewall, router and switch (with a baseline: an account added later is flagged) and who is logged in right now, from where. Asks per session [k]ick / [l]eave (default kick when it is not from --team) and per account [d]isable / [k]eep (default disable when new since the first run). Never kicks its own login or disables the login account; checks each change after; undo per account (from NW-01's saved copy, no hash copied)

name: Network device hardening
what_it_does: Per firewall, router and switch: telnet and plain HTTP management off, management limited to the team and this box, SSH v2, idle timeout, default SNMP communities removed, MikroTik MAC telnet off, logs to Splunk, time server, login banner. Asks per finding; changes go through one open session, a new login is tested and you confirm from another machine before it is saved, else it is put back; undo per device
you_give_it: Team addresses; log and time server

name: Firewall ruleset
what_it_does: Puts named bt- rules at the top of the network firewall (Palo Alto, Cisco ASA, FortiGate, MikroTik, a Linux router; pfSense/OPNsense as web GUI steps): the team allowed, any address to each scored box on its scored ports only, ping in, everything else coming in blocked and logged. Optional (default no): the servers may only start connections to DNS, NTP and listed places; threat prevention. Asks per rule; checks every scored service before and after and puts everything back at once if one stops answering; you confirm against the scoreboard; undo per device and --remove
you_give_it: Scored boxes and ports (typed, a .txt list, or from an SH-03 scan); team addresses

name: Device change watch
what_it_does: Reads every firewall, router and switch every few minutes (the same show commands as NW-01) and compares it with a trusted baseline (NW-01's copy, an earlier watch, or read now). Each added, removed or moved line is shown once with its section, HIGH/MED, what it may mean and a suggested undo that is never sent; asks whether the changes were ours (only a person can say so). Shows when a change goes away; a changed SSH host key is HIGH; secrets masked
you_give_it: Devices; how often and how long

name: Linux alerts
what_it_does: Asks what to watch, takes a baseline, then checks once or every N seconds: accounts, passwords, admin groups, sudo/PAM/preload files, cron and timers, boot units, running services (logging stopped = HIGH), SSH keys, new listeners with the process behind them, NEW outgoing connections (reverse shells) and new addresses on admin ports, SUID files, web roots, kernel modules. One plain-words alert per change, HIGH first, sendable off the box
you_give_it: Team addresses; interval; extra web roots

name: Linux session & command logging
what_it_does: Reads the auth log and (if on) auditd: logs every login, source address, failed/brute-force attempt, sudo/su, and every command, to per-category log files. Flags web shells (a command run by the web-server user, a process running from /tmp or a web root, and injection/known-shell requests in the access log). Console alerts, but an admin allowlist keeps your own teams activity quiet. Pairs with LX-40.

name: Linux persistence sweep
what_it_does: Finds persistence in 13 areas (cron, systemd, boot hooks, SSH keys, shell startup files, preload, accounts/sudo, PAM, kernel, planted files, processes, web shells, mail hooks); asks what to scan; with --apply asks about removing each finding (moved to quarantine, revert timer)
you_give_it: Areas to scan; what to remove

name: Log shipping to Splunk
what_it_does: Receiver: a Splunk TCP/UDP syslog input (its own app) on the Splunk box. Sender: rsyslog sends the system logs and the service log files it finds (web, mail, Roundcube, databases, audit) to Splunk, disk-buffered; config checked with rsyslogd -N1; a test line to search for
you_give_it: The Splunk box address and port

name: Rootkit and malware scan
what_it_does: Hidden processes (/proc vs ps), hidden ports (/proc/net vs ss), hidden or rootkit kernel modules and taint, core programs that do not match their package, rootkit file paths, programs in /dev, fake kernel threads, miners, sniffers; ClamAV/rkhunter/chkrootkit when present (install offered); kill or quarantine asked per finding

name: AppArmor confinement
what_it_does: Puts apache2, nginx, php-fpm and mariadb/mysql under AppArmor in three steps: complain (logs only), learn (adds the normal logged accesses, never a shell or download tool), enforce (with a check that the service still answers and a revert timer). Uses the package's own profile when there is one; SELinux mode shown on Red Hat.

name: Safe security updates
what_it_does: Package sources (unknown, unsigned) and held packages first; then pending updates grouped by service (ssh, openssl, sudo, web, php, database, mail...), security apart, kernel and non-security default skip. Saves the old packages, keeps your config files, checks ports / web page / database after each group and offers to roll that group back. Offers restarts for services on old library code.

name: Windows alerts
what_it_does: Alerts on new logons, new accounts, new admins, new services and tasks, cleared logs, Defender or firewall turned off.

name: Windows persistence sweep
what_it_does: Finds persistence in 8 areas (scheduled tasks, Run keys, startup folders, Winlogon, services, WMI subscriptions, debuggers, local admins and RDP users); HIGH ones offered for removal, MED kept by default; tasks disabled, values removed with the old value in the undo, files quarantined; revert timer. The Windows twin of LX-42

name: Brute-force and spam banning
what_it_does: Asks the limits, ban length, services and who never to ban; reads SSH, FTP, mail, web-login and PAM failures and bans addresses over the limit in nftables/ipset/iptables with a ban that ends by itself. Never bans your team, the scoring engine, this box or the gateway (reports them). Reports spam from a compromised mailbox. Dry run by default, --list, --unban, --unban-all

name: Shell library (lib.sh)
what_it_does: Shared code for every Unix script: options, dry run and apply, logs, backup with undo, protected list, exit codes, password generator, quarantine. To do: the shared countdown-and-revert helper

name: PowerShell library (lib.ps1)
what_it_does: The same for PowerShell 2.0 and later, plus a CSV writer and WMI fallbacks. To do: the shared countdown-and-revert helper

name: Build step
what_it_does: Pastes the library into each script so every file in dist/ runs standalone (copy one file), and writes dist/MANIFEST.sha256 so each script can check it was not changed. --check fails when dist/ is out of date
